2026-10-08_update_aws_gfs_dead_end_confi.hypothesis_tested: Whether the public AWS Open Data GFS mirror (s3://noaa-gfs-bdp-pds, scripts/gfs_aws_source.py -- the same source now confirmed working for LIVE CB acquisition) could be queried for HISTORICAL cycles around the 395 INDOFLOODS event dates that fall on/after 2015-02-01 (the 0.25-degree operational GFS's earliest possible existence), as an alternative to the local D:\ archive referenced above.
2026-10-08_update_aws_gfs_dead_end_confi.method: Live HTTPS S3 ListBucket queries (?list-type=2&prefix=gfs.<YYYYMMDD>/00/) against noaa-gfs-bdp-pds.s3.amazonaws.com -- not inferred, not assumed.
2026-10-08_update_aws_gfs_dead_end_confi.result: The bucket's real retention floor is 2021-01-01 (KeyCount=0 for 2020-12-15 and earlier dates tested; KeyCount=1 for 2021-01-01 onward). Re-filtering processed/indofloods/indofloods_grid_events.csv for Start Date >= 2021-01-01 returns ZERO unique event dates -- the INDOFLOODS dataset's events end in 2020, entirely before this bucket's retention window begins.
2026-10-08_update_aws_gfs_dead_end_confi.conclusion: DEAD END, confirmed with live evidence, not merely assumed: the AWS GFS operational mirror cannot be used to backfill historical dynamic features for any existing INDOFLOODS event, no matter how much of it is downloaded. This route is closed, not still-open-but-unfinished.
2026-10-08_update_aws_gfs_dead_end_confi.the_real_remaining_option: ERA5 reanalysis (ECMWF Copernicus Climate Data Store, free/public, hourly, 1940-present, 0.25-degree) is the only free/public source identified so far whose temporal coverage genuinely overlaps the 2791 INDOFLOODS event dates (1965-2020). It has NOT been acquired or integrated yet -- this is the next concrete step for FF V2's dynamic-feature gap, not the AWS GFS path above, which is closed.
